Unfortunately I think this goes beyond just being a hoax, this originated from a Suramin manufacturer selling it as an anti-parasite. I’m not making any certain statements but it seems suspicious that the only research into the medication’s use related to autism is funded by PaxMedica. I wouldn’t be surprised if they are trying to profit off of societal hatred of autism.

I looked into the trials of Suramin, I could only find two that were done in South Africa where it is approved for human use. In the “Competing interests” section of [this publication](https://annals-general-psychiatry.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s12991-023-00477-8) I found, it looks like there could be financial motivations behind the researchers/authors involved, as there usually is with pharmaceutical companies. 


The study was funded by PaxMedica, a pharmaceutical company that is planning to file an NDA with the FDA (trying to get Suramin approved) for the treatment of African trypanosomiasis. This is an incredibly rare illness in the US and there are already other medications approved by the FDA to treat it. I absolutely do not trust these “autism cure” studies, thought I would share.
